flags.observation: Both style variants are single-genre (Bollywood dance; cumbia), no genre fusion. BPM, one voice, seven instruments and groove word fit.
Thesis aims at "bankers" as people rather than institutions or money mechanics; deck note wants satire on institutions.
"one breath per card" is production meta that could sit in any track of the series; carries no deck content.
"cartels washed over a trillion in one year" lifts card 33's lore; beat 9 then repeats it almost word for word.
freeze/froze/frozen appears four times in frame and openers (beats 1, 3, 4, 5) outside card text.
"The Euro Snake, it paved the way" doubles the subject and stumbles in one breath.
"Planners took notes" is abstract; of eleven openers only "champagne" and "macaw" draw on artwork images (Tip 5 thin).
BIS Manager attribution dropped, so "we don't know who uses a hundred dollar bill" becomes the narrator's claim; no closing punctuation.
"non-compliant trades blocked" recites the power text almost verbatim as a rule.
"fine you" turns the card's customers into you and drops the misinformation reason, losing the card's claim.
"by the BIS" lands unexplained because beat 17 lost the BIS attribution; listeners get an acronym with nothing to hold.
"No mob, one macaw" uses the image word, but the listener never sees what the macaw does; reads cryptic.
"Bankers hate this" is a clickbait wink; Tip 4 asks for a straight face.
Outro punch is concrete and calls back the croissant, but mostly reprises beats 3 and 4 rather than adding a new statement.
